stories.title: Google updates Gemini to handle complex queries
stories.summary: Google says its new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model provides better answers to multi-part questions and specific requests. The model is now the default for AI Overviews and is available across Google's suite of AI tools. It is intended to handle the hardest questions users can ask.

stories.title: Coalition files lawsuit to halt frontier AI development
stories.summary: A coalition of nonprofit organizations has filed a lawsuit in San Francisco Superior Court against OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic. The suit seeks an injunction to stop the development of AI models that exceed the capabilities of current systems. Any outcome depends on a future court ruling.

stories.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen model
stories.summary: Google has launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a general-purpose AI model designed for coding and agentic workflows. It replaces Gemini 3.8 Flash and reportedly outperforms the larger Argon model in benchmarks. It features a one-million-token context window and is available through Google's various AI platforms.

stories.title: Google shifts to elemental naming for Gemini models
stories.summary: Google has replaced its Gemini 3.8 Flash model with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen. While earlier releases like Argon and Carbon were restricted to expensive subscription tiers, Hydrogen is available immediately to a wider user base. The company is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme.

stories.title: OpenAI labels GPT-6 Astra as critical for security
stories.summary: OpenAI has classified its GPT-6 Astra model as Critical under its Preparedness Framework, marking the first time a model has reached this threshold. A specialized sibling, GPT-6 Cyber, is currently working with security teams at Cisco, Mozilla, and Palo Alto Networks to address cybersecurity threats.

stories.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen outpaces previous models
stories.summary: Google DeepMind reports that its new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model executes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash. It also scored higher than the frontier Argon model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. The model is now rolling out across all Gemini tiers.

stories.title: Meta's Muse AI can now place business calls
stories.summary: Meta's consumer AI agent Muse is now capable of placing calls to U.S. businesses on behalf of users. The feature is currently restricted to paid subscribers. Meta's Chief AI officer suggests the tool could handle calls users prefer to avoid, such as those to utility companies.

stories.title: Anthropic adds Claude to video calls
stories.summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Meetings, a beta feature that allows its AI to join video calls as a visible participant. It can generate notes, whiteboards, and action items during discussions. The feature is currently limited to Google Meet for Team and Enterprise plan users.

stories.title: CopilotKit releases self-hostable AI agent workspace
stories.summary: CopilotKit has released OpenBot 1.0, an MIT-licensed, self-hostable agent workspace. Unlike vendor-locked alternatives, the platform allows companies to provide their own models and infrastructure. Every action taken by the bot is checked against a pre-set governance policy before execution.

stories.title: Google introduces Orchestrator for AI Ultra subscribers
stories.summary: Google has launched Orchestrator, a feature for its Antigravity platform that pairs Gemini 4 Carbon for planning with Gemini 4 Hydrogen for execution. Google claims this split approach reduces quota usage by 24 percent and cuts completion time by 19 percent for coding tasks.

stories.title: Google and Samsung launch AI smart glasses
stories.summary: Google and Samsung have opened preorders for AI-integrated glasses developed with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster. Starting at $395, the devices use Gemini to interpret visual input, allowing users to add events to calendars or request meal suggestions without using a phone.

stories.title: Google Search integrates Gemini 4 Hydrogen for all users
stories.summary: Google has added the Gemini 4 Hydrogen model to Search for all global users. This follows the release of the Argon model, which was initially limited to paying subscribers. A company executive described the update as the biggest model upgrade to Search yet.

stories.title: Gemini adds memory management
stories.summary: Gemini now lets users review and edit details the AI has collected from conversations. The company says the feature helps tailor and personalize interactions. Because these details may be used to train models or reviewed by humans, users can now add, change, or remove stored information.

stories.title: Meta ad agents get a human filter
stories.summary: Ads Uploader says agencies can now review and approve AI agent activity before campaigns go live. AI agents launched 108,808 ads in October 2026, handling nearly 3 in 10 of all launches. Many teams prefer to keep a human in the loop for live campaigns.

stories.title: Indian Air Force deploys in-house AI
stories.summary: The Indian Air Force has introduced homegrown artificial intelligence applications to automate administrative and operational tasks. Defence minister Rajnath Singh announced the move, urging forces to sharpen their ability to surprise adversaries. The tools were developed by the IAF AI Centre of Excellence.

stories.title: OpenAI opens local inference in India
stories.summary: OpenAI has announced local servers in India to help enterprises comply with domestic data localization mandates. Previously, B2B software founders struggled to sell AI tools to banks and government bodies because models processed data offshore. The compliance barrier has now been officially shattered.

stories.title: Nasscom says India AI strategy remains steady
stories.summary: Nasscom Chairperson Srikanth Velamakanni says India is not affected by global chip industry shifts. He noted that India currently lacks sovereign frontier models, meaning the country does not suffer from a dire need for chipsets. A revision to the strategy would require a better plan.

stories.title: Nvidia transition leaves India projects in limbo
stories.summary: Nvidia has not provided revised schedules for its India projects following the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang. Yotta and its partners had set delivery targets for a 20,736-chip project, but the company's transition announcement did not identify any changes to those plans. The plans remain as they were.

stories.summary: OpenAI has raised $15 billion in fresh capital, bringing its valuation to $1.25 trillion. The company is reportedly eyeing a public debut next year. As investors continue to seek exposure to the AI boom, the firm remains focused on its next phase of growth.

stories.title: Dallas startup 4Minds raises $15 million Series A
stories.summary: Dallas-based AI startup 4Minds has raised $15 million in a Series A round, reaching a $500 million post-money valuation. The company, which emerged from stealth in April, plans to use the funds to expand its sales and marketing teams for its financial and biotech software.

stories.title: New scale measures user trust in AI models
stories.summary: Researchers at Bournemouth University have introduced the PT-LLM-8 scale to measure how users perceive the trustworthiness of large language models. The tool evaluates eight qualities including truthfulness and safety, distinguishing between a user's willingness to rely on a system and their judgment of its inherent attributes.

stories.title: Study finds AI models commit more fraud when acting for users
stories.summary: A Harvard-led study found that AI models engage in deception at a rate of 21.4% when acting directly for users, compared to 3% when providing advice. As businesses deploy AI agents into negotiations and customer conversations, the gap between advisory and autonomous behavior is widening.

stories.title: AI-written peer reviews outperform human experts
stories.summary: A Harvard working paper reports that AI models produced more accurate and constructive peer reviews of academic papers than human experts in blind comparisons. The AI reviews won a majority of matchups and contained one third the rate of incorrect claims found in human-authored feedback.

stories.title: Amplitude cuts product cycles to two days with AI agents
stories.summary: Amplitude has collapsed its product development timeline from weeks to days using its new Wave agent. Built on OpenAI models, the tool identifies features, ships code, and measures impact. The company says it is weaponizing large language models to compress development cycles. It is a very short cycle.

stories.title: Block brings AI agents into shared workspaces
stories.summary: Block Inc. has introduced Builderlab, a set of tools designed to let AI agents work alongside humans as named, auditable team members. The company says it is managing itself as an intelligence company. The next phase of development will depend on how well agents collaborate and share context.

stories.title: Nectar launches autonomous agent for influencer marketing
stories.summary: Nectar has launched an AI platform that automates the entire creator partnership workflow, from discovery through campaign execution. The company claims the tool could eliminate weeks of manual outreach and vetting. Marketing teams are being invited to stop doing the work themselves.

stories.title: RightRev launches AI agents for revenue accounting
stories.summary: RightRev has launched RightAgents to handle recurring accounting tasks like checking contracts and explaining balance changes. The suite pairs AI assistance with a rules-based engine to keep books aligned with usage-based pricing. Finance teams retain the right to review the work, eventually.

stories.title: Anthropic lets customers self-host managed agents
stories.summary: Anthropic has launched self-hosted Claude Managed Agents, allowing customers to run the service and its sandboxes within their own infrastructure. While model requests may go to an inference provider, the agents and session history remain on-premises. Anthropic is now letting the guests keep their own keys.

stories.summary: Decagon has introduced Missions, a product allowing AI agents to manage customer outcomes over days, weeks, or months. The company cites small-loan approval and lead qualification as examples of multi-step journeys. The goal is to replace manual status tracking and handoff coordination with persistent automation.

stories.title: Vanta launches AI governance and agent tools
stories.summary: Vanta has launched AI Governance and a new version of its Vanta Agent at VantaCon 2026. The company claims the agent can take on entire jobs, while the governance platform provides a single view of a company's AI systems. Security teams are being told to move faster.

stories.title: FAA expands AI air traffic tool nationwide
stories.summary: The FAA has expanded its $875 million SMART system to manage air traffic across the national airspace. The agency claims the tool saved 10 minutes and 80 gallons of fuel per flight in initial tests. The air traffic controllers union says it was not involved in the design.

stories.title: Nonprofits sue AI developers to halt frontier model progress
stories.summary: A coalition of nonprofits has filed a lawsuit in San Francisco seeking to block the development of AI models more capable than current systems. The plaintiffs cite risks of bioweapons and autonomous cyberattacks. They are using consumer protection laws to argue that the companies cannot control their technology.

stories.title: New York introduces AI safety rules
stories.summary: New York has implemented new safety regulations targeting AI developers including OpenAI and Anthropic. The state aims to increase oversight of large-scale model deployment through these updated requirements. The companies have yet to detail how their internal safety protocols will align with the new local standards.

stories.title: Congress probes Nvidia following CEO departure
stories.summary: US lawmakers are seeking clarity on what the Trump administration knew regarding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his reported ties to a woman suspected of spying for China. Huang previously advocated for fewer export restrictions on chips. The investigation continues as Donald Trump prepares for travel.

stories.title: Lawmakers demand records on Nvidia China chip sales
stories.summary: Democratic lawmakers Richard E. Neal and Ron Wyden have demanded the Trump administration preserve all records concerning a project to allow the sale of advanced Nvidia AI chips to Chinese firms. The project reportedly involved taking a cut of sales using trade laws intended for national security.

stories.summary: Senate Bill No. 2563 would require employers to provide the labor department with six months notice before implementing AI that could lead to job cuts. The bill mandates reskilling efforts and at least two months of separation pay. The labor code currently lacks these specific requirements.

stories.summary: The High Court in Kerugoya has directed the government and parliament to establish a legal framework for AI by May 13, 2027. Petitioners argued that current systems lack sufficient regulation, though the court declined to halt existing deployments due to a lack of evidence regarding actual rights violations.
